title: Bartholomew's Funny Song
markdown:
It was a very rainy day. The sky looked like a big, grey blanket, and raindrops went pitter-patter on the window. Inside their cozy home, up in the big oak tree, lived Cora and Maple. They were two little squirrels with busy tails.

Cora, with eyes like shiny buttons, was putting her acorns in order. "This one," she chirped, holding up a nice round acorn, "is for Tuesday!" She gave it a little rub with her soft paw.

Maple, whose fur was the color of warm bread, was putting smooth stones in a line. "And this one," she whispered, placing a stone by a piece of moss, "is for looking at the clouds. It looks like a sleepy sheep, don't you think?" Her fluffy ears wiggled as she imagined sheep in the sky.

Down in the garden, where the ground smelled nice and wet, lived their friend, Mrs. Bramble. Mrs. Bramble was a wise old hedgehog with glasses that sparkled. She was getting ready for the big Spring Parade. She was making her flowers extra shiny for the parade float. She hummed a quiet, happy song.

This year, a new musician was joining the parade! It was Bartholomew Bumble, a little mole. Bartholomew had a small trumpet made from a flower stem. He also had a very proud little hat that sat right on his head. He had spent all winter, down underground, writing a new song. He thought it was the best song ever.

Bartholomew was very excited to share his song. He thought it was just right for marching.

One rainy afternoon, Bartholomew waddled up to Cora and Maple’s tree. He tapped his trumpet on the bark. “Cora! Maple!” he called out. “Can I play you my new song? It’s called ‘The Happy Hopping Song’! I practiced it every single day!”

Cora and Maple, their paws a little sticky, ran down to a low branch. Mrs. Bramble, hearing Bartholomew, walked over too. Her glasses sparkled in the soft light.

Bartholomew took a breath that made his whiskers wiggle. He puffed out his chest, and his hat wiggled. Then, he began to play. His song was neat and tidy. It had a beginning, a middle, and an end. It went: *Ta-ta-ta, TUM! Ta-ta-ta, TUM!* It was very proper.

Cora watched Bartholomew’s face. Maple listened very closely. Mrs. Bramble nodded her head.

"Well?" said Bartholomew, his nose twitching. "Isn't it a fine song for the parade? It will make everyone march with a happy step!"

Cora, who was always kind, said, "It's very… neat, Bartholomew! Every note is just right!"

Maple added, her voice soft like the wind, "Your beat is perfect, Bartholomew. It's very steady."

"Steady?" Bartholomew blinked his little mole eyes. He looked a bit confused. "But it’s supposed to be exciting! It’s supposed to make you want to hop and skip! It’s supposed to be fun!"

Sometimes, the most correct music isn't the most fun music. Bartholomew felt a little worried. He had tried his very best. He thought his song was perfect, but his friends didn't feel the happy hopping.

Bartholomew wasn't sure what to do. He thought maybe his trumpet needed a little encouragement. Or maybe he needed to get his music muscles ready.

So, Bartholomew put his trumpet down. He took a big breath. Instead of a loud note, out came a funny, bubbly *GULP-GLUG!* It sounded like a happy drink.

Cora and Maple’s eyes grew wide. Then, giggles came out, like bubbles from a fizzy drink. *Gulp-glug!*

Bartholomew tried again, a bit braver this time. A little squeaky *EEEP-eep-eep!* came out, like a tiny mouse that bumped its toe. Cora laughed, and her tail thumped. Maple clapped her paws together, smiling big.

Then, Bartholomew made more funny sounds! A low, rumbling *Bzzz-rumble-rumble* that sounded like a happy bee dreaming of honey. A high, sweet *Twee-hee-hee!* like a bird singing in the rain. And then, a surprised little *WHOOPS-a-daisy!* that made Bartholomew jump.

The squirrels laughed and laughed. Their tails thumped with happiness. Mrs. Bramble let out a big chuckle that shook her prickles. "Oh, Bartholomew!" she said. "Those sounds are wonderful! They make me want to dance!"

Bartholomew looked at his happy friends. A warm, bright feeling spread through his heart. He realized these silly sounds made everyone feel joyful and ready for fun.

Bartholomew had a new idea! It was a wobbly, wonderful idea, just like the funny sounds.

"You know," he said, his hat tilted happily, "maybe ‘The Happy Hopping Song’ needs a funny little hello before it starts. Something to make everyone’s toes tap!"

The next day, at the Spring Parade, all the animals gathered. Bartholomew stepped forward. Everyone waited for his proper song. But first, Bartholomew took a breath and made a cheerful, bubbly *GULP-GLUG!* The animals gasped, then giggled. Then came a bright *Twee-hee-hee!* which made the little mice wiggle their whiskers and dance. Then, Bartholomew played his song, but now it was even better! It had the happy surprise of the silly sounds. It made everyone want to march with a happy bounce.

And so, Bartholomew the mole learned that the best music is not always the most proper. Sometimes, the funniest sounds from a happy heart make our smiles bloom, just like the flowers in spring.
characters: Cora the squirrel, Maple the squirrel, Mrs. Bramble
